_doc: Explicit link overrides for [[slug]] links and aside slugs in data/articles/*.json. Read by tools/article_gate.py and js/article.js (arColor), and consulted BEFORE the canonical names and the alias tables (data/graph/aliases.json, data/aliases.json), so an entry here wins. Use it only for names those tables do not resolve or resolve wrongly. Each entry: to = canonical slug in data/graph/names.json, or null to show the word as plain text (a pigment or historical name that is not a color in our data; never invent one); label = the word the reader sees on the link (the original word is kept, the page opened is the canonical color); reason = why (required).

rose-madder.label: rose madder
rose-madder.reason: Rose madder is a real pigment (a pale madder lake), but the 2026-10-08 Maerz & Paul merge filed the dictionary's 'Rose Madder' swatch (#E32636) as a near-duplicate alternate name of Imperial Red, a different color. Linking it would open Imperial Red under the madder article, so it is shown as plain text.

yinmn-blue.label: YInMn blue
yinmn-blue.reason: YInMn blue is a 2009 pigment (a compound of yttrium, indium and manganese oxides). The data merge filed the library's YInMn Blue screen swatch under Dusk Blue, which the same sentence already links, so linking the pigment would send two links to one page. Shown as plain text.

paris-blue.label: Paris blue
paris-blue.reason: Paris blue is a trade synonym of Prussian blue (the article's aka list says so). The library's Ridgway 'Paris Blue' swatch was merged into Lapis Lazuli, which is a different color, so the synonym is mapped to the pigment's own color.
